title: DABUS
summary:
DABUS (Device for the Autonomous Bootstrapping of Unified Sentience) is an artificial intelligence system created by Stephen Thaler. It reportedly conceived of two novel products: a food container constructed using fractal geometry which enables rapid reheating, and a flashing beacon for attracting enhanced attention.

On 17 September 2019, Thaler filed an application to patent a "Food container and devices and methods for attracting enhanced attention," naming DABUS as the inventor. This sparked a series of legal battles around the world over whether an AI system can be recognized as an inventor under patent law. On 24 June 2021, the South African Companies and Intellectual Property Commission accepted the patent application, making it the first patent granted for an AI invention.

The European Patent Office rejected the applications on 27 January 2020 on the grounds that the application listed an AI system and not a human as the inventor. The Board of Appeal confirmed that under the EPC the designated inventor has to be a person with legal capacity. In Australia, the Full Court of the Federal Court held that only a natural person can be an inventor for the purposes of the Patents Act. The UK Supreme Court upheld earlier decisions that DABUS could not be named as inventor because it is not a person. New Zealand's IPONZ decided that DABUS could not be an actual devisor of the invention as required by the Patents Act 2013.

The Artificial Inventor Project (AIP) is a global legal initiative headed by Professor Ryan Abbott dedicated to pursuing intellectual property rights for inventions and creative works generated autonomously by AI systems. The project coordinates a series of pro bono test cases worldwide, aiming to prompt law reform and public debate on how IP law should accommodate non-human creators. The DABUS case remains a landmark in the ongoing debate about AI and intellectual property law, with most jurisdictions concluding that current patent laws require inventors to be natural persons.
